items.title: Terry Gibbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2001 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: You know Louella Parsons, you know that name?

ctx.x: But they want you in the studio.

Yeah. Well I was going to do this in the studio. This was done in the studio. But they want you in the studio, not rehearsing in a hall somewhere. So I had all this music. In the meantime there was a club that was going to close call The Seville. And the movie columnist called Eve Star took a liking to how I played and she knew the club owner at The Seville, and they were going to go out of business. They tried Latin, they tried all this, they had to try jazz. So they hired me with a quintet. They said five…

pieces of music and I said, “On this song on letter B, Conte you play a hundred choruses, on C Frank Rosolino, you have two thousand choruses,” we had to open it up. We’ll make backgrounds you know. And so we started to walk out to play, and there were 300 people packed in the club with a line waiting to get in. And you saw faces like Fred McMurray and Ginger Rodgers. All these movie stars. And all the musicians in town. So I called the band back in the dressing room. I said, “We’re starting a band tonight, but…
